note: The ten worst single days in the Dow Jones Industrial Average, measured close to close. IMPORTANT: these are drawn as candle BODIES ONLY. A real candle's body runs open to close and its wicks show the intraday high and low; reliable intraday ranges for 1899–1932 are not something we have, so the figure shows the close-to-close move and its caption says so. `pct` is the day's percentage change; `nextLabel` describes what the index did afterwards and is only filled in where we can state it plainly.
source: Standard record of the DJIA's largest one-day percentage declines. What came next: 1987 — the Dow closed the year at 1938.83 against 1895.95 at the end of 1986, i.e. UP on the year, and regained its August 1987 peak in August 1989. 2020 — the low came a week later on 23 March 2020 at 18,591.93, and the Dow closed above 30,000 for the first time on 24 November 2020, a new record. 1929 — the slide continued to 41.22 on 8 July 1932, 89 percent below the September 1929 peak, and the old peak was not regained until 23 November 1954.

afters.headline: The worst day ever recorded.
afters.next: The Dow finished that same year UP on the year. It was back at its August peak within two years.
afters.verdict: A record-breaking crash, and by New Year it had mostly stopped mattering.

afters.headline: The second worst.
afters.next: The bottom came a week later. Eight months after that the Dow closed above 30,000 for the first time in its history.
afters.verdict: A world-stopping pandemic, and the chart had healed by November.

afters.headline: Third and fourth.
afters.next: It kept falling. For nearly three more years, to 89 percent below the peak. The old high was not seen again until 1954.
afters.verdict: Almost exactly the same size of day. Twenty-five years to get back.
